chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Coming to Denver in the 1960s and the Clef Club's beginnings
summary: Horace moved from California about twelve years earlier, found jam sessions at a Washington Avenue club with Shelly Rhythm and Ron Washington, and bassist Chuck Roberts, then an after-hours club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Now you said you've been in Denver for 12 years?
Uh-huh. And you came here from the west coast?

Yes, I came here from California. I'd heard about the mile high climate and all, and I just had met some people in California, and they said, "You should come to Denver," one of these things, and I said, "Well, the first chance I where time off, that were chance I might get when I get a little free moment, I'll drive out, alone, and case the place and see, you know, so sure enough, I came out here. I ran into some good musicians connected with a club called the -- on Washington Avenue this particular club was, called the Clef Clinton Club. And this was the beginning here, and I've met quite a few friends down there. They used to have jam sessions there.
And I met the fellow that played drums there, actually managed a club, called Shelly Rhythm.

Shelly was my -- probably my first -- well, I mentioned the Mel Torme drumming thing, and when I was in, I think, my first year of high school or even still in junior high school, I heard Shelly play. And that's what got me into this business too.
Yeah, Shelly's been in Denver. He knew all the musicians. And we had the Sunday jam sessions there. He gave me a job playing piano in a group that consisted of Ron Washington on tenor saxophone.
I've worked with Ron. Yeah, I've played jobs with him.

(Unintelligible). And they had an excellent little bass player. You know, I can't think of that guy's name now. It's been so long. But, gee, he was a great little bass player. He was an excellent reader, and he helped me in quite a few ways during that time. There was a lot of things that, meeting people, and we got to be good friends, and there was a group that came through Denver one time wanting a bass player, and old silly me, I recommended him. They heard him, and they took him. And he's living right now in Reno, Nevada, and playing. Chuck is his first name. It just came to me. Chuck Roberts, that's his name. Yeah. And, oh, he played real good.

And we used to get off in the mornings and go and sip coffee somewhere and talk nothing but music, you know. And he introduced me to a lot of the musicians in Denver, and they used to come in and they'd sit in with us and jam. And a lot of times this particular club was the haven for musicians that would come in from out of town and couldn't sleep nights, you know. It ran pretty late, you know.
This was after -- the first after hour club. They later moved downtown -- at 18th and Broadway.
